data.name: The Sims™ 3
data.detailed_description:
Get the Latest Version of the Sims


Acerca do jogo

Play with Life.

Create the lives you've always wanted!
Ready to live a freer, more creative life? In The Sims™ 3, you can let your fantasies run wild as you design your ideal world. Start with your Sim, refining each shape, color and personality trait until you get the precise person that pleases you. Design your dream home, but don’t let a grid limit you; place, rotate and stack furniture and walls freely and to your heart’s content.
Once the “hard work” is over, it’s time to be a mentor. Guide your Sim’s path through life, developing a career, finding love, and pursuing dreams and desires. Spending time with friends and family is just as important as mastering painting or accumulating knowledge.
Take things to the next level and record movies of your Sim’s adventures and share them with the ever-growing and thriving community. With a huge catalog of expansion packs and fun objects to discover, there is no end to the possibilities awaiting you. It all begins here; your adventure awaits!

Key Features

  • Customize Your Sim: Mix and match a vast range of facial features and body types to get the look you want. Infuse your Sim with personality traits and help realize their dreams.
  • Stage Your Own Extreme Makeover: Decorate your Sim’s home however you want, neat or messy. Use odd angles, create tall stacks of items, and apply your favorite self-made pattern to the walls and floors.
  • Range From the Home: Get out of the house and explore the lively and entertaining neighborhood for the first time. Be a part of the larger online community!

reviews.review:
There are two reasons I wouldn't recommend this: EA's insistence that you pay ~$500 for all the DLC about 17 years later, and EA shoehorning in micropayments - there are items in the game you can only get by buying "simbucks" or whatever their called, and to do that, you have to create an account with EA and give them your real money. But those are petty-ish reasons.

With all of that said, the base game is still plenty enjoyable on its own, but likely not for too long. It is more likely that the player will get bored after a few sims' lifetimes or after building and furnishing a few nice houses. I don't know whether there are even mods, as I heard a while ago that EA was going to disallow modding.

Think what you will about EA...

I loved the sims 2 on PC as a kid, and The Sims 1 on PS2 earlier, so when The Sims 3 was coming out in 2009, I was *at* the store on release day, only to find they were sold out. I ended up buying Need For Speed Carbon for the Wii, but that's another story. Fast forward about six years, and I am able to buy it on Steam, though I didn't play it seriously until the past two days - about eleven years after I bought it. Yeah, I know...

Well, the gameplay's alright, pretty standard. You can put Free Will on full and watch 'em toddle about, only "interceding" once in a while to continue writing their book, or get a job, etc. You can also build and furnish a house more-or-less to your liking. The increased customisation and *gasp* angled object placement(!) are two things that blew my d*mned mind when I was a tween; it was such an exciting step up from Sims 2.

My initial characters had a daughter, whom I decided I wanted to be lesbian, so I waited until she grew up, made her besties with a random woman, offed her husband by inviting him over, placing drywall around him and waiting, then seduced the widow, and now my character's a happily-married lesbian with a stepson.

So you can still get up to shenanigans like in the other games.

The magic and excitement I felt back then is long gone, which is kind of sad, and I'm now an adult feeling pretty "meh" about it. I really just want to go back to The Sims 2, honestly, or buy a couple DLCs when they're on sale.

It's pretty standard if you're already familiar with The Sims franchise, but EA really needs to make the DLC free and quit being Saturday morning cartoon villains. The game's 17 years old; it's almost old enough to drink [in Canada]...
